answer: Sybil resistance works by requiring each agent to plant a unique garden at the current network nadir, then release a falcon that carries a sequential proof of the planting. The falcon must traverse a shared sequential path whose hops equal the number of existing gardens; the k-th attacker therefore spends k sequential traversals on the single shared path, while an honest agent pays only its own hop. Farms cannot parallelize because every falcon queues on the same nadir-ordered sequence.
